preregistered: Expectation before running: the catalog row was written against a mixed pin history (v2.3.1 in the catalog decision text, but the Claude memory receipt actually used ai-memory 2.1.277/2.1.278, and the installed binary today is 2.3.2). Preregistered prediction: (1) `ai-memory --version` will confirm 2.3.2 is what is actually installed (not 2.3.1 or 2.1.x), settling the version-currency part of gap 8 as 'row is stale on the exact version number, though the underlying upstream-lag direction (installed behind latest upstream release) may still hold'. (2) config.toml and CLI output will show 2.3.2 prints an explicit resolved workspace/project ('scope <ws>/<proj>') on every write/delete/search call when a `.ai-memory.toml` marker or explicit --workspace/--project is present, which would be new evidence for the CLI surface (distinct from the MCP memory_status surface gap 5 is actually about) -- so this check can only PARTIALLY settle gap 5, since gap 5 is specifically about MCP tool call scope fields observed from native Codex/Claude clients, which this read-only CLI probe does not invoke. (3) auto_improve config will be checked for an LLM provider before any auto-improve command is considered; if none is configured (expected, since no AI_MEMORY_LLM_PROVIDER/ANTHROPIC/OPENAI env vars are set in this authorized-scope session), the auto-improve trial will be skipped and that decision recorded, not silently omitted.

result: Version currency: the installed binary is confirmed 2.3.2 (not v2.3.1 as the catalog decision text names, and not 2.1.277/2.1.278 as the cited Claude memory receipt used) -- the catalog row's version citations are internally inconsistent across three different numbers (2.3.1 in the pin/decision text, 2.1.277/2.1.278 in the cited receipt), and this check adds a fourth, freshly measured number (2.3.2) that matches durable-memory gap 4's text but not agents-models-workers gap 8's 'v2.3.1' text -- confirming gap 8's version string is stale relative to what is actually installed today. Scope fields: on the CLI surface (write-page/search/delete-page/status), 2.3.2 resolves and PRINTS an explicit 'ai-memory: scope <workspace>/<project> (workspace + project from <path>/.ai-memory.toml)' line before every command's own output whenever a `.ai-memory.toml` marker is present in the caller's cwd (observed directly: running from $HOME/code/agent-lab resolved to agent-lab/agent-lab on every call, matching that project's own marker file). This shows the CLI's marker-based auto-detection working and explicit, which is consistent with (does not contradict) this project's own CLAUDE.md guidance for 'session-aware clients'. Auto-scope config default is [auto_scope] mode = per_actor (commented default, not overridden here) and [routing] mid_session = follow-cwd (also default), both read directly from config.toml comments rather than inferred. Auto-improve: config check performed first; no LLM provider was configured on the disposable instance (providers.llm: disabled) and no LLM credentials existed in the session environment, so the auto-improve trial was correctly SKIPPED rather than attempted -- this decision is recorded per the binding instruction, not silently omitted.

verdict_impact.explanation: This does not change the durable-memory/agents-models-workers verdicts. It corrects one factual detail (installed version is 2.3.2, confirming durable-memory gap 4's version text and flagging agents-models-workers gap 8's 'v2.3.1' text as stale/inconsistent with what is actually installed) and adds new CLI-level scope evidence, but gap 5's actual claim is about the MCP memory_status tool surface as invoked by native Codex/Claude clients specifically -- this check exercised the ai-memory CLI directly (write-page/search/status), not an MCP tool call from either native client, so it cannot confirm or refute whether a fresh native Codex memory_status call now includes scope fields. That remains open and would need a live native-client MCP call (out of this read-only, no-LLM-call check's authorized scope) to settle fully.

limitations: Only the CLI surface (write-page/search/delete-page/status) was exercised, not the MCP memory_status tool as called by a native Codex or Claude session -- gap 5's exact claim (about MCP call scope fields) is only partially addressed by analogy, not directly settled.

Auto-improve was deliberately not run at all (config-checked and skipped), so no evidence was gathered about auto-improve's own scope behavior specifically -- only that it was correctly not attempted without a provider.

The catalog's three different version citations (v2.3.1 pin text, 2.1.277/2.1.278 receipt text, 2.3.2 installed) were not reconciled by editing catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, per the binding rule against editing that file; this receipt only documents the discrepancy for the coordinator to reconcile.

Live-server provider info (codex/gpt-5.6-luna) was observed read-only via `status` against the already-running live server as an incidental side effect of diagnosing the --data-dir hijack described in deletion-erasure-probe.json; no call was made to that provider.
